sections.content:
Interesting! Now the stamp area shows:
- Rows 34-38: all purple (50 cells)
- Rows 39-43: white on left, purple on right, diagonal pattern (35 white, 15 purple)
This is the SAME pattern as before! The purple diamond stamp turned the top 5 rows purple and added the diagonal pattern on the right side of the bottom 5 rows.
So the stamping mechanic seems to be:
- The shape is projected onto the stamp area
- Cells covered by the shape get the selected color
- Different rotations cover different cells
Let me now systematically explore all 4 rotations to understand which cells each covers. I'll track the state after each stamp.
Current state: 65 purple, 35 white (same as after the first two SPACE actions)
Let me try rotating to different orientations and stamping with WHITE to see which cells get affected. The key insight is that I need to find which rotation covers the bottom-left white cells (the triangular pattern).
Let me try LEFT to rotate the shape, then SPACE with white to see the effect.

<parameter=code>
# Let me systematically explore all 4 rotations
# Current shape is diamond (after 1 RIGHT from rectangle)
# Let me rotate LEFT to get back to rectangle, then try all rotations

# First, rotate LEFT to get rectangle
action(['LEFT'])

# Check shape
seg = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'p' and 80 < n['pixels'] < 90:
        print(f"Shape after LEFT: pixels={n['pixels']}, hash={n['hash']}, boundary={n['boundary']}")

# Now stamp with white rectangle
action(['SPACE'])

ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
print("\n=== After white rectangle SPACE ===")
for i in range(34, 44):
    line = ascii_lines[i][27:37]
    print(f"Row {i:2d}: {line}")
white_count = sum(1 for i in range(34, 44) for j in range(27, 37) if ascii_lines[i][j] == 'W')
purple_count = sum(1 for i in range(34, 44) for j in range(27, 37) if ascii_lines[i][j] == 'p')
print(f"White: {white_count}, Purple: {purple_count}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
